_comment: Canonical building catalogue for Defenders of the Realm — the five gameplay buildings the player raises in Elarion (Crystal Mine, Pet House, Arcane Tower, Workshop, Farm). Shared by the React v1 engine and the Unity v2 port. The Unity loader (BuildingCatalog.cs) deserializes each entry into a typed BuildingDef record and Building.cs consumes HP from it.

_sources.buildingSpotsTs: defenders-of-the-realm/src/modules/village/buildings/BUILDING_SPOTS.ts (ids, KayKit mesh urls, ring radii, resource yields, scale targets)
_sources.villageSliceTs: defenders-of-the-realm/src/state/slices/villageSlice.ts (TOWER_TIER_COSTS — the only canonical crystal-cost reference; 120 crystals to build a tower)
_sources.canonStrings: defenders-unity/Assets/StreamingAssets/Data/Canonical/canon-strings.json (displayName keys: crystalMine / petHouse / arcaneTower / workshop / farm)
_sources.portSpec: defenders-unity/docs/v2-unity-port-spec.md (Part 4 buildings.json schema row, Week 4 Village systems)

_authoringNotes.sourcedFromReactV1: id, displayName (canon-strings key), descriptionKey (en.json key), model (KayKit medieval mesh name, stripped of the React 'building_*_color' prefix/suffix per village-buildings-overhaul-spec §3), footprint hex size category (derived from §4 scale convention).
_authoringNotes.authoredDefensible: hp / maxHp and crystalCost are AUTHORED. React v1 has no per-building HP or build-cost table — its five buildings are FIXED map placements, not player-built, and only towers carry a crystal cost (TOWER_TIER_COSTS = 120 crystals build). Values below were authored: defensive structures (Arcane Tower) sit highest HP+cost; resource/economy buildings (Crystal Mine, Farm) lowest cost so the economy can bootstrap; Workshop/Pet House mid. All are tuning constants the owner may rebalance — flagged in docs/port-notes/week4-buildings.md and surfaced to the integrator. JSON wins over ScriptableObject (port spec Part 4).
_authoringNotes.footprint: hex footprint size category — 'small' (1 hex tile), 'medium' (cluster), 'large' (the tall Arcane Tower silhouette). The build menu's hex-tile validity check reads this; large footprints need more clear neighbours.
_authoringNotes.displayName: displayName is a KEY into canon-strings.json, NOT a literal — the build menu resolves it through BuildingCatalog/CanonStrings so the canon names are never typed inline (port spec Part 4). STOP: THE WO-840 NAMING INVERSION RECORDED IN THE NEXT SENTENCE IS RETIRED (2026-08-23, WO-1161 follow-up) - it is kept only so a reader recognises the old crossing, and it must NOT be re-applied. structures-catalog.json is the SINGLE naming authority; names are derived from what a building DOES (vendors.json), so id 'forge' sells WEAPONS and reads 'Forge', id 'armorer' sells ARMOUR and reads 'Armorer', and id 'workshop' is not a vendor and reads 'Crafting Station'. canon-strings.json was corrected to match in the same edit, which self-corrects the 'workshop' and 'forge' rows here; the 'armorer' row was re-pointed from the 'blacksmith' key to the new 'armorer' key. The 'blacksmith' canon key survives unreferenced rather than being deleted (nothing else reads it, and a missing key renders '[[missing:<key>]]' onto a nameplate). RETIRED TEXT FOLLOWS - WO-840 naming inversion (re-verified 2026-08-08): the ids are NOT their nameplates — id 'workshop' is the WEAPONS shop and reads 'Forge', id 'forge' is the ARMOR shop and reads 'Armorer', id 'armorer' reads 'Blacksmith'. Every displayName key here MUST exist in canon-strings.json AND be unique across rows: a missing key renders the literal '[[missing:<key>]]' straight onto the nameplate (VillageStrings.Resolve) and a shared key gives two buildings one name. v3 fixed both at once — the armorer row duplicated the forge row's key, and 'market'/'jeweler' had no key at all.
_authoringNotes.crystalsPerWave: WO-856: the Crystal Mine's per-wave payout CURVE, indexed by (level - 1) and clamped into range: L1=1, L2=2, L3=4. The level comes from PlacedStructure.level (the one persisted per-instance level), NOT from any field on CrystalMine. Rung count must not exceed structures-catalog.json mine_crystal repo.maxLevel: [yield-reachable-at-founding] in BuildingUpgradeRegression fails if it does, or if the first rung is 0 (a structure that delivers nothing at its founding level). A bare scalar here read-migrates to a flat curve.
